meaning: a false impression or deceptive appearance that misleads the senses or the mind
sentence: The still water created the illusion of a second range of hills below the first.

meaning: a confused, complicated and embarrassing situation, especially a public or political one
sentence: The transfer order dragged the whole department into a political imbroglio.

meaning: filled or permeated with a quality, feeling or idea
sentence: His years at the academy had imbued him with a quiet sense of duty.

meaning: copied the speech, manner or appearance of another person or thing
sentence: The younger cadets imitated his stiff, precise way of marching.

meaning: to come into a country other than one's own in order to settle there permanently
sentence: Her grandparents chose to immigrate to Canada in the 1970s.

meaning: lacking modesty, whether by boasting or by offending against decency
sentence: It was an immodest boast for a man who had never seen action.

meaning: to kill or destroy as a sacrifice, especially by fire
sentence: Ancient rites required the priest to immolate a goat before the shrine.

meaning: the condition of having little or no money
sentence: His impecuniousness forced him to walk to college every day.

meaning: impossible to pass through or enter; also, impossible to understand
sentence: The battalion halted before an impenetrable wall of thorn scrub.

meaning: unable to be appeased, softened or turned aside from a purpose
sentence: He faced an implacable opponent who would accept nothing short of surrender.

meaning: to call into question or attack as false the honesty, motives or validity of something
sentence: You may disagree with his decision, but do not impugn his motives.

meaning: called into question or attacked as false the honesty, motives or validity of something
sentence: The defence lawyer impugned the honesty of every witness in turn.

meaning: acting suddenly on a sudden urge, without forethought
sentence: One impulsive remark in the interview cost him the appointment.

meaning: to attribute a fault, crime or motive to someone, often without proof
sentence: It is unfair to impute cowardice to a man who was simply following orders.

meaning: unable to express oneself clearly or fluently in speech
sentence: Nervousness left him inarticulate at the very moment he needed to explain himself.

meaning: glowing white with heat; also, brilliantly bright or blazing with anger
sentence: The old bulb glowed with a soft incandescent light.

meaning: just beginning to appear or develop, and still in its earliest stage
sentence: The doctor spotted an incipient infection before it could spread.

meaning: so firmly set in a bad habit that no correction or reform is possible
sentence: He is an incorrigible gossip, and no warning has ever slowed him down.

meaning: too extraordinary to be believed; also, remarkably good
sentence: The rescue team covered forty kilometres in an incredible eleven hours.

meaning: not liable to fail, decay or become defective
sentence: The regiment prided itself on an indefectible record of loyalty.

meaning: a lack of tact or refinement, or a coarse and improper act or remark
sentence: It was an indelicacy to raise money matters at the funeral.

meaning: extreme poverty and want of the means of living
sentence: Years of drought reduced the whole village to indigence.

meaning: persuades someone to do something, or brings about a particular state or effect
sentence: A warm bath induces sleep more reliably than any tablet.

meaning: the allowing of a pleasure to oneself or another, or the lenience that permits it
sentence: A second helping of sweets was his one indulgence of the week.

meaning: too great, intense or sacred to be put into words
sentence: Standing at the pass at dawn, he felt an ineffable calm.

meaning: unfairness or lack of even-handedness in the way people are treated or things are shared out
sentence: The report exposed the inequity of paying women less for identical work.

meaning: a general rise in prices that reduces the purchasing power of money; also, the act of filling something with air
sentence: Rising fuel prices pushed inflation to its highest level in a decade.

meaning: showing clever originality and inventiveness in devising or making something
sentence: She devised an ingenious pulley to lift the water drums onto the roof.

meaning: harmful to something, or openly unfriendly towards it
sentence: Constant interruption is inimical to serious study.

meaning: an indirect remark that hints at something disparaging or improper
sentence: He never made a direct accusation, but the whole speech was thick with innuendo.

meaning: placed or fitted something into something else
sentence: The clerk inserted an extra clause into the contract without telling anyone.

meaning: lacking flavour, vigour or interest; dull and tasteless
sentence: The soup was warm but insipid, and no one asked for a second bowl.

meaning: unable to pay one's debts as they fall due
sentence: The firm was declared insolvent after its last creditor went to court.

meaning: to arrange financial cover against loss or damage by paying a premium to a company
sentence: He decided to insure the new motorcycle against theft and fire.

meaning: a person who takes part in a conversation or formal dialogue
sentence: The diplomat found his interlocutor courteous but unwilling to concede anything.

meaning: the act of stepping into a situation in order to alter what would otherwise happen
sentence: Timely intervention by the sentry prevented a serious accident.

meaning: made something known indirectly, hinting at it rather than stating it outright
sentence: She never said so plainly, but she intimated that she would resign.

meaning: so severe or offensive that it cannot be endured
sentence: The heat inside the tin shed became intolerable by noon.

meaning: to accustom someone to something unpleasant so that they come to bear it without distress
sentence: Two winters on the glacier had inured him to the cold.

meaning: spoke or wrote against something with bitter hostility
sentence: The old colonel inveighed against the sloppy turnout of the new recruits.

meaning: an animal that has no backbone, such as an insect, worm or jellyfish
sentence: A prawn is an invertebrate, though its hard shell suggests otherwise.

meaning: having a habit so long established that it is unlikely ever to change
sentence: He is an inveterate reader and never travels without three books.

meaning: not governed by reason or sound judgement; in mathematics, a number that cannot be written as a ratio of two integers
sentence: His irrational fear of lifts made him climb nine floors every morning.

meaning: the state of having no bearing on the matter under discussion
sentence: The witness's long account of his childhood was dismissed as an irrelevance.

meaning: hesitating and unable to settle on a course of action
sentence: The commander could not afford to look irresolute in front of his men.

meaning: impossible to recover or to put right again
sentence: Deleting the only copy caused an irretrievable loss of data.

meaning: to throw goods overboard to lighten a vessel, or to abandon something no longer wanted
sentence: The crew had to jettison part of the cargo to keep the boat afloat.

meaning: relating to courts of law, to judges, or to the administration of justice
sentence: The matter was settled by a judicial order rather than a departmental one.

meaning: the judges and courts of a country taken collectively as a branch of the state
sentence: An independent judiciary is the chief safeguard of a citizen's rights.

meaning: the raised stone or concrete edge of a pavement where it meets the road
sentence: He tripped over the kerb while stepping off the pavement.
